text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000537 bills 99215 at roughly double the all-provider rate in every complexity stratum; the few returned charts support the billed levels but are too thin to settle the question.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The by-complexity table shows about twice the all-provider 99215 share at every condition count, including 0 and 1 conditions. Because the excess persists after holding complexity fixed, a sicker panel does not explain it, and the pattern is consistent with a provider-level coding habit. Against that, none of the 6 documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level. That sample is far too small to clear the provider, and the documentation has warning signs of its own. Supported claim C0296764 is a 99215 for a patient with no chronic conditions and an upper respiratory infection (J06.9), documented as high MDM with no time recorded, and the same note is flagged for a problems signal. The returned notes also show some repeated time entries, two notes claim moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab or test line on the claim, and no audit trail was received to rule out cloned or templated notes. A reviewer should first pull charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims (for example C0296805, C0297696, C0298054, C0298917), check whether high MDM is credible for simple diagnoses like back pain and abdominal pain, and request the EHR audit trail to test for templated documentation."}
